requirements.reason: Permission addressed to producers about packaging. This implementation uses one representation; nothing follows for a verifier to check.

requirements.note: Exclusion rules may read only issuer attributes or target attributes from the frozen target directory; any other input is a profile error.
Reading: transport acknowledgements are not receiver-side records; they are accounted in the input accounting, outside |R|.
Each obligation lists every attempt that carries evidence; report_check refuses a named attempt missing from that list.

-01 finding S5.4-1 (Disposition when no issuer-side observation exists for an instruction in the population) is resolved in -02: Section 5.4 lines 746-758 define a missing required issuer observation: the instruction stays accounted for, dispatch is NOT_ESTABLISHED, the obligation INDETERMINATE by default. Implemented.

requirements.reason: Addressed to the issuer side (recording a failed emission). The verifier consumes such a record and keeps it as an instruction-level diagnostic; that behaviour is tested under S5.4-8. -01 finding S5.4-5 (result of an emission that failed before the issuer boundary) is resolved by Section 5.4 lines 760-766.

requirements.finding: Disposition of the obligations of an instruction whose only issuer record is an unscoped failed emission
readings: (a) INDETERMINATE: the required issuer observation at the boundary is missing (5.4 default)
(b) UNCONFIRMED: an expected obligation without a matching receiver observation
requirements.implemented: (a), with dispatch NOT_ESTABLISHED and the failure kept as an instruction diagnostic
requirements.why: 5.4 makes a missing issuer observation INDETERMINATE by default and forbids consuming the failure as proof of non-delivery; UNCONFIRMED is defined by the absence of a receiver observation only, while here the issuer side itself is not established.

requirements.note: Reading: an observer absent from the trust configuration gives INDETERMINATE (unresolved trust binding); an observer bound to another target gives an invalid receiver record and leaves the obligation as it was.

-01 finding S5.7-3 (NO_EFFECT is used in two dimensions and the control-effect vocabulary is not defined) is resolved in -02: Sections 4.4 (lines 635-639) and 4.5 (lines 653-658) put enforcement NO_EFFECT and control-effect NO_EFFECT in separate namespaces; the -01 reading (b) stands.

-01 finding S5.8-1 (Deadline-elapsed negative observation: UNCONFIRMED or EXPLICIT_FAILURE) is resolved in -02: Section 5.8 lines 833-836 and 9.1 lines 1692-1694: deadline elapsed leaves UNCONFIRMED with a deadline diagnostic; the -01 reading (a) stands.

requirements.reason: MAY. This verifier defines no timely-delivery claim kind; the deadline diagnostic stays on the obligation, which remains UNCONFIRMED (Section 5.8).

requirements.finding: How a record names the uniqueness scope of its identifier, and which scopes are valid
readings: (a) a record or frozen instruction may carry its own identifier scope; equal strings from different scopes are different identities
(b) only scopes the profile lists are valid; a record of another scope is INVALID
requirements.implemented: (a): an optional identifier_scope; a record of a scope the frozen population does not hold stays outside the population and blocks PASS through the population check
requirements.why: 5.1 asks the profile to define one uniqueness scope; 5.10 speaks of several valid scopes without saying how a record conveys which one it belongs to.

requirements.note: Reduction rule: the profile's published precedence over the seven dispositions; every applicable disposition stays listed.

requirements.reason: Addressed to whoever runs reconciliations. Each report names the exclusion rule versions it applied (S5.11-4) and the digest of the report before it, so a changed rule shows as a separate report; a single verifier run cannot see whether a producer rewrote another run.

requirements.note: -01 finding S5.11-3 (record class of a receiver record that addresses an expected obligation but does not confirm it) is resolved in -02: matched means correlated (Section 5.11 lines 939-947, Section 6.1 lines 1212-1220). A receiver record of an attempt the issuer never emitted is now correlated, not orphan.
Receiver records of an unclosed instruction have no expected obligation to correlate with and are ORPHAN, with the instruction class named.
Known targets of an unclosed resolution are reported as a subscope with its narrower scope stated, outside the Delivery Obligation population.

requirements.finding: Class of an issuer binding that contradicts the frozen Required Target Set
readings: (a) INVALID: the issuer record lacks the binding required for structural validity
(b) CONFLICT: two verified inputs (issuer record and frozen target set) make irreconcilable claims
requirements.implemented: the profile classifies it as INVALID or CONFLICT; the example profile says INVALID. Unresolved, ambiguous and stale references are always INDETERMINATE (the -01 finding S5.12-1 is resolved)
requirements.why: 5.12 names INVALID for a missing required binding and CONFLICT for irreconcilable verified records; a binding to a different set is neither missing nor a second record of the same kind.

requirements.reason: Addressed to a relying system's operational policy (fail-safe, retry, escalation). The report exposes the four states; choosing the local response is outside this verifier.

requirements.note: -01 finding S6.1-1 (Issuer-side identifier reuse with different content) is resolved in -02: Sections 5.10 (lines 879-885) and 6.1 (lines 1190-1196) define SUBSTITUTION for issuer-issuer reuse within one uniqueness scope; the -01 reading (a) stands, now with the records named.

-01 finding S6.2-1 (Parent result of an instruction with zero obligations) is resolved in -02: Section 6.2 lines 1252-1254: parent confirmation of a terminal empty set is NOT_APPLICABLE or absent; the -01 reading (a) stands (null).
Duplicate selection rule: earliest observed time, then record id; the discarded record names the selected one.

-01 finding S6.4-1 (Unit of a Delivery Obligation) is resolved in -02: Sections 2 (lines 354-360), 4.2 (lines 574-579) and 5.1 (lines 687-693) fix the base obligation as instruction times required target; the -01 reading (a) stands.

-01 finding S6.4-3 (Instruction-level equation has no class for a target resolution that fails or stays open) is resolved in -02: Sections 5.11 (lines 983-990) and 6.4 (lines 1365-1374) add the disjoint class target_resolution_unclosed; the instruction equation now has three terms and no obligation is created for an unclosed instruction. Implemented: class renamed, no obligations, one equation.
The matched class is a primary class; its confirming and non-confirming subdivision is published beside the equation and not added to it.

requirements.finding: How an exclusion-rule violation becomes a positive FAIL condition
readings: (a) a positively established invalid or outcome-adaptive exclusion is a FAIL condition the profile may declare
(b) such an exclusion only prevents PASS
requirements.implemented: (b) for this implementation: it finds exclusion-rule violations only as profile declaration errors, under which no FAIL is derived, and refuses a profile that declares them a FAIL condition; the dispositions EXPLICIT_FAILURE, SUBSTITUTION, CONFLICT and INVALID are declared true or false by the profile
requirements.why: 6.5 asks how exclusion-rule violations are handled in the FAIL conditions, while 5.11 says such an exclusion prevents PASS and only a predeclared positive condition produces FAIL; the text does not say what evidence makes the violation positive.

requirements.note: -01 finding S6.5-3 (Which dispositions are positive failing conditions for FAIL) is resolved in -02: Section 6.5 lines 1420-1426: the profile publishes and freezes its positive FAIL conditions; no universal mapping. Implemented as fail_conditions in the profile.

-01 finding S6.5-4 (Excluding an obligation 'before population construction' cannot depend on its disposition) is resolved in -02: Sections 4.2 (lines 565-572) and 5.11 (lines 921-926): exclusions are frozen before receiver evidence and never depend on a disposition; the -01 reading (a) stands.

-01 finding S6.6-3 (Co-exposure when no relying-party claim is requested) is resolved in -02: Section 6.6 lines 1487-1492: with no stronger claim requested, the corresponding claim is the minimal structural statement under the named profile, cutoff and structural rules; the -01 reading (a) stands, the claim scope now names the profile.
